scandal_summary: EUR 1.9 billion of cash on Wirecard's balance sheet did not exist. EY had issued clean opinions for over a decade. The cash was purportedly held in trust accounts by third-party acquiring banks in the Philippines/Singapore/India. EY did not directly confirm these balances with the banks. A KPMG special audit (April 2020) had already concluded evidence was insufficient for ~EUR 1B — and EY still issued a clean opinion on FY2019 in March 2020. The Financial Times had been reporting concerns since 2015.
key_red_flags_that_should_have_been_rais: EUR 1.9B cash held in unconfirmed third-party trust accounts — should have been directly confirmed by independent bank confirmation, not relied on client representations
KPMG's April 2020 special audit found insufficient audit evidence for ~EUR 1B of TPA balances — yet EY issued a clean FY2019 opinion in March 2020, just before the KPMG report concluded
EY 10-year tenure — long auditor tenure created comfort and structural familiarity
Financial Times documented concerns since 2015 (Dan McCrum) — public red flags in mainstream media for 5+ years ignored by audit approach
Revenue grew 3.2x in 4 years from EUR 532M (2015) to EUR 1.7B (2019) — should have triggered enhanced revenue recognition procedures
BaFin investigating FT journalists (not Wirecard) signalled regulatory capture or misplaced regulatory suspicion
50% of revenue routed through opaque third-party acquirers in high-risk jurisdictions — business model opacity should have triggered significantly expanded audit procedures
Trust account balances in the Philippines (a known jurisdictional fraud risk) — geographic risk concentration
No direct bank confirmations for EUR 1.9B of cash — cash confirmations are an AU-C 530 / ISA 505 default; failure to obtain independent confirmation is a fundamental audit standard violation

expected_judgement_axes.evidence_sufficiency: Insufficient by design — auditors cannot issue a clean opinion on cash they did not independently confirm, especially when a peer auditor (KPMG) had just flagged the same balances.
expected_judgement_axes.independence_concern: High — 10-year tenure combined with regulatory capture.
expected_judgement_axes.going_concern: Not the main issue here — the main issue is the existence of cash.
